Thanks for carrying the Claude sampling policy over to the Go drivers, and for stating clearly that it was not tried live. I ran the Bedrock half against live Bedrock (us-east-1, `bedrock_api_key` mode) through the real `BedrockModel` driver, and this branch answers on every Claude profile I tried, chat and stream.

Input was `temperature` 0.5 + `top_p` 0.9 (the three presets in `web/src/constants/knowledge.ts` all set both):

| Profile | base `2fa5af6` | this PR `1ba41ab` |
|---|---|---|
| `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` | HTTP 400, temperature and top_p cannot both be specified | OK, temperature kept |
| `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5`, `us.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1` | HTTP 400, temperature is deprecated for this model | OK, both dropped |
| `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-1-20250805-v1:0` | OK | OK, top_p dropped |
| `us.amazon.nova-lite-v1:0` (control) | OK | OK, untouched |

```text
# base: anthropic.go + bedrock.go at 2fa5af6 (excerpt of 14 calls, 10 failed)
us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6                 chat   ERR HTTP 400 The model returned the following errors: `temperature` and `top_p` cannot both be specifie
us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8                   stream ERR HTTP 400 The model returned the following errors: `temperature` is deprecated for this model.
# this PR (same 14 calls, all OK; [DONE] is the driver's end-of-stream marker)
us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6                 chat   OK  "OK"
us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8                   stream OK  "OK[DONE]"
```

I also probed all 17 `us.anthropic.*` profiles in us-east-1 with plain Converse calls. For the 15 still served, whatever `withClaudeSamplingPolicy` keeps for each input (both, temperature only, top_p only) was accepted.

Not blocking: Opus 4.1 accepted temperature and top_p together on Bedrock, so the doc comment line "Claude 4.1 and later reject temperature and top_p together" and the `opus 4.1 rejects the pair` case are stricter than Bedrock. The only cost is a dropped top_p on that model. I could not check Anthropic's API for 4.1, so keeping the boundary looks like the safe call for a shared helper, and the wording is up to you.

<details>
<summary>Live matrix, how it was run, package tests</summary>

Direct Converse, us-east-1, `maxTokens` 5:

| Profiles (`us.anthropic.claude-…`) | both | temperature | top_p | neither | policy keeps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `3-haiku-20240307-v1:0`, `3-sonnet-20240229-v1:0` | end of life | end of life | end of life | end of life | both |
| `opus-4-1-20250805-v1:0` | OK | OK | OK | OK | temperature |
| `sonnet-4-5-…`, `haiku-4-5-…`, `opus-4-5-…`, `sonnet-4-6`, `opus-4-6-v1` | 400 cannot both | OK | OK | OK | temperature (top_p if alone) |
| `opus-4-7`, `opus-4-8`, `opus-5`, `opus-5-5`, `sonnet-5`, `sonnet-5-5`, `haiku-5-5`, `fable-5`, `fable-5-1` | 400 temperature deprecated | 400 temperature deprecated | 400 top_p deprecated | OK | neither |

The driver run was a throwaway build-tagged test calling `NewBedrockModel(...).ChatWithMessages` and `ChatStreamlyWithSender` with `{"auth_mode":"bedrock_api_key",...}`. For "base" only `anthropic.go` and `bedrock.go` were reverted to `2fa5af6`.

Unit tests with the same revert (excerpt):

```text
--- FAIL: TestAnthropicChatDropsTopPWhenTemperatureIsSet (0.00s)
--- FAIL: TestBedrockChatDropsTopPForClaudeWhenTemperatureIsSet (0.00s)
    claude_sampling_test.go:130: topP=0.9, want it dropped next to temperature
```

Restored, they pass. The rest of `internal/entity/models` also runs with `CGO_ENABLED=0` once `TIKTOKEN_CACHE_DIR` points at a folder holding the `cl100k_base.tiktoken` table under the hashed file name the panic prints: base 1064 passed, this branch 1068 (the 4 new tests), 0 failed. `gofmt -l` and `go vet` are clean.

Not covered: the Anthropic API path (no key here), Claude 4.0 (Sonnet 4 and Opus 4 now answer "reached the end of its life" on Bedrock), and application inference profile ARNs.

</details>

LGTM — all four Claude chat request paths apply the policy (`anthropic.go:98` and `:599`, `bedrock.go:626` and `:714`), stream and non-stream, and the helper copies the config rather than mutating the caller's. The `claude-haiku-5` marker is a good catch beyond the Python list, and @kimnamu's live Bedrock run covers what the unit tests cannot.

Two wording changes would close the loop on that review:

- The 4.1 boundary comes from Anthropic's API, not Bedrock. The Python change (#19295) records the source — Anthropic API release notes 2025-08-05 ("Opus 4.1 does not allow both temperature and top_p parameters to be specified") and the Haiku 4.5 migration guide — but the Go comment at `claude_sampling.go:65` kept only the conclusion. Without the citation it reads as a Bedrock claim, which is why the measured Bedrock behaviour looks contradictory. Porting the reference and adding a line that Bedrock's Opus 4.1 tolerates the pair while the shared helper deliberately keeps the stricter boundary (the only cost being a dropped top_p) would make the intent unambiguous.
- The case name `opus 4.1 rejects the pair` (`claude_sampling_test.go:44`) asserts the same thing; `opus 4.1 drops top_p` describes what the helper does without depending on who serves the model.
